entries.title: MLB considering playing a game at Grand Teton National Park
entries.summary: <p>Major League Baseball has reached out to the federal government about the possibility of one day staging a game in western Wyoming's Grand Teton National Park, an idea quickly met with resistance from environmental groups and others.</p><p>MLB and the players' association have played a handful of regular-season games away from the 30 big league ballparks in recent years, including in the Iowa corn fields made famous by the movie "Field of Dreams."</p><p>An MLB official familiar with the discussions confirmed Monday that the league approached the Trump administration about possibly hosting a game in a national park. The person spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because the league hadn't authorized comment on the matter and said it was among several ideas MLB has explored.</p><p>A White House official said MLB asked the administration whether hosting a game at a national park would be possible but emphasized it was not a presidential directive and was not driven by the administration. The National Park Service has not granted any permits, said the official, who spoke on condition of anonymity because there was no authorization to speak on the record.</p><p>MLB's special event games have included games at Dyersville, Iowa, in 2021, 2022 and 2026, with another scheduled next August between Boston and Kansas City.</p><p>In addition, regular-season games were played at Rickwood Field in Birmingham, Alabama, in 2024 and at Bristol Motor Speedway in Bristol, Tennessee, in 2025, and games have been held since 2017 in conjunction with the Little League World Series in Williamsport, Pennsylvania.</p><p>MLB also has played international games in London; Mexico City and Monterrey, Mexico; Seoul, South Korea; Sydney; and Tokyo; plus some in San Juan, Puerto Rico.</p><p>Grand Teton includes a commercial airport — the busiest in Wyoming — and a vast expanse of Jackson Hole bottomlands with spectacular views of the Teton Range. There is no shortage of flat terrain where a temporary ballpark could be built.</p><p>The possibility of building a baseball field on national park land quickly raised a host of questions.</p><p>"It's abhorrent," Mike Gierau, a Democratic state senator and baseball lover who represents Jackson and nearby Grand Teton, wrote in a text message. "Baseball is the American game. The national parks are America's greatest idea. But a national park is to be protected for its undeveloped and scenic values."</p><p>Environmental groups also came out against the idea, first reported by The Washington Post.</p><p>"Americans want to see protections for our national parks and public lands strengthened. Bulldozing these lands for a baseball stadium does the opposite, destroying the magnificent landscapes that millions of people come to experience," Chris Kassar, the group's Wyoming director, said in a statement.</p><p>A message left with Grand Teton officials seeking more information wasn't immediately returned.<br></p>

entries.title: Hagen Smith will open up a White Sox bullpen game in Game 1 of Wild Card series against Astros
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON – Two years after being their fifth overall pick, rookie left-hander <b>Hagen Smith</b> will start the first White Sox playoff game in five years. Just like they planned, right?</p><p>Well, there’s some nuance.</p><p>Smith has been <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/08/24/white-sox-hagen-smith-brian-bannister-will-venable-2024-draft-jac-caglianone-konnor-griffin-trey-yesavage-pitching-development-pete-crow-armstrong" target="_blank" ><u>working as a reliever since being called up in August</u></a>, three innings represents the longest outing of his career and he won’t be improving upon it in Tuesday’s Game 1 against the Astros. Manager <b>Will Venable</b> said the Sox are throwing a bullpen game–as are the Astros, started by right-hander <b>A.J. Blubaugh</b>.</p><p>Even their oft-used strategy of an opener setting up a bulk pitcher who works four-to-five innings is more conservative than what the White Sox have planned.</p><p>“You might have a starter, a young starter, go four, five innings, perhaps even more than that,” said general manager <b>Chris Getz</b>. “But if we can get higher end two, three-inning outings from some of these guys, we're going to lean in that direction.”</p><p><b>Sean Burke </b>and <b>David Sandlin </b>split the only two starts of six innings or longer that the Sox had in all of September. The club used an opener or bullpen game an MLB-leading 31 times in 2026, and have primed their pitching staff for a relay race of one-to-three-inning appearances that will define their Wild Card series strategy.</p><p>“Kind of being doing it all year, right?” Sox pitching coach <b>Zach</b> <b>Bove</b> told the Sun-Times. “The message to all the guys is to be ready for multiple situations. That’s it. We’ll communicate as best we can to where they’re going to be. But at the same time, it’s maybe not going to be the traditional way of going about it.”</p><p>In a best-of-three series where the risk of the bullpen wearing down is lessened, the White Sox see it as a means to an end. They don’t think their fans, nor 90-year-old chairman <b>Jerry Reinsdorf </b>will fret too much about the aesthetics.</p><p>“Not if it helps us win games,” retorted Getz.</p><p><b>The likely AL MVP plays for the other side</b></p><p>Tapping Smith, when he’s held left-handed hitters to a .194/.256/.278 batting line this season, smacks of a pitching strategy built around unfavorable matchups for Astros slugger <b>Yordan Alvarez</b>, who led the American League in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601) this season.</p><p>“As great as Yordan is, he's not the only really good hitter in their lineup, so you can't just totally say, ‘Hey, we're not going to let Yordan beat us,’ and walk him every time,” said Venable.</p><p>Except the Sox kinda have. Alvarez went 4-for-20 with a double against the Sox this year, but he scored five runs in seven games because they walked him at a 27.6% clip. If avoiding Alvarez doesn’t work, a bullpen game could ensure he faces a left-hander almost every time.</p><p>“He hasn't really kind of hurt us, so we feel generally good about the plan,” Bove said. “But obviously he is a great hitter.”</p><p><b>Meidroth should be good to go</b></p><p>After not playing in the final series–outside of a pinch-hit double on Saturday–due to a sore left hamstring, second baseman<b> Chase Meidroth</b> is expected to be able to play on Tuesday.</p><p>“He's going to be maybe not 100%, but as close to a normal version of Chase as we can get right now,” Venable said.</p>

entries.title: A look at the top contenders for the Sun-Times high school football player of the year
entries.summary: <p>Kameron McGee caught a screen pass from Sam Holcomb in the third quarter of Brother Rice’s win against Mount Carmel in Week 6.</p><p>The junior defensive superstar beat two defenders, then raced past three more for a 33-yard touchdown that gave the Crusaders the lead for good.</p><p>It was an eye-opening moment that showed how much the exceptional athlete could impact every phase of the game. It was a Player of the Year-caliber moment.</p><p>McGee is one of the best college prospects in the country, the best junior prospect in the nation according to some evaluators, and has been on the POY radar since the preseason.</p><p>Brother Rice’s win against the Caravan and McGee’s starring role certainly helped his case. McGee also had four tackles, four hurries, a sack and a TFL in the game.</p><p>Lincoln-Way East quarterback Jonas Williams was an easy pick for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-football/2025/12/17/jonas-williams-chicago-sun-times-player-of-the-year-lincoln-way-east-usc" >Sun-Times Player of the Year</a> last season. Williams set state records for career passing yards and career TD passes.</p><p>No player this year has that level of historic resume, but it is an uncommonly strong year overall, with multiple excellent contenders after six weeks.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Kam McGee also scores touchdowns. Brother Rice’s defensive star catches a pass from Sam Holcomb, sheds tacklers and scores a 33-yard TD. <br><br>What a game. The Crusaders lead Mount Carmel 28-24 in the 3Q. <a href="https://t.co/rUdF9KWNpb">pic.twitter.com/rUdF9KWNpb</a></p>— Michael O'Brien (@michaelsobrien) <a href="https://x.com/michaelsobrien/status/2103663569376051507?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>McGee is certainly in the race. Here’s a look at some other top contenders.</p><h3>Israel Abrams, Montini</h3><p>The senior quarterback is carrying a huge load for the Broncos. Abrams, a Miami recruit, threw for 411 yards against Nazareth and 398 yards in the Week 6 loss to St. Rita. He’s thrown 18 touchdown passes so far this season.</p><p>Abrams will finish the season with POY numbers, and his put together a career very worthy of the award. Another state title run will be a key factor in Abrams’ candidacy.</p><h3>Jake Thies, Fenwick</h3><p>The Iowa recruit is the best full-time two-way player in the area. Thies, the breakout star of last season’s football state finals, is lighting up the stat sheet as a running back and defensive back. He has 65 carries for 574 yards and 18 catches for 255 yards with nine total touchdowns. Defensively, he’s added 56 tackles, 5 TFLs, and an interception.</p><p>The Friars were ranked for about half the season. Team success will play a major factor in Thies’s POY chances. Fenwick has big regular-season games remaining against Providence and Carmel, so Thies has two major opportunities to sparkle before the playoffs even begin.</p><h3>Jake Nawrot, Hersey</h3><p>The Huskies didn’t play a Week 6 game because Wheeling forfeited, so Nawrot’s stats cover just five games. The Kentucky recruit is 87-for-127, throwing for 1,321 yards, 17 touchdowns, and no interceptions.</p><p>Hersey’s final regular-season game against Prospect will be a major opportunity for Nawrot to open more eyes. A very deep run in the Class 7A playoffs will be key for Nawrot’s POY chances.</p><h3>Ben Peterson and Bennett Konkey, Geneva</h3><p>The two biggest surprises on the list. Peterson, an Eastern Michigan recruit, has thrown for 1,847 yards and 22 TDs with just two interceptions this season. Bennett Konkey, Peterson’s top receiver, is also a major POY candidate. The Illinois recruit has 46 catches for 961 yards and 13 TDs this season. The Vikings’ Week 6 win against Batavia was a major resume booster for both players.</p><h3>Michael Vander Luitgaren, Batavia</h3><p>The numbers are huge for Vander Luitgaren, a Wyoming recruit. He’s 126-for-164 passing for 1,801 yards and 23 TDs with five interceptions. He’s also rushed for nine touchdowns. Batavia has a major win against Maine South, but Vander Luitgaren will likely need a Class 7A state title to win POY, especially after the loss to Geneva.</p><p><b>Other contenders to watch include Mount Carmel receiver Marshaun Thornton, Maine South quarterback Jameson Purcell, and Loyola linebacker Will Mettee.</b></p>

entries.title: Bears LT Braxton Jones leaves Eagles game with injury
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> left tackle Braxton Jones walked to the locker room in the third quarter after hurting his right knee <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-eagles-notes-rookie-dillon-thieneman-first-interception-andy-dalton" target="_blank" >against the Eagles</a>. He was at first ruled questionable to return and soon thereafter called doubtful.</p><p>Jones was emotional as he went to the ground and was helped to the blue injury tent. </p><p>He was replaced by Theo Benedet, who played occasionally last week and in the first half Sunday to keep Jones fresh.</p><p>Jones dealt with a knee injury in August, right around the team he started to pull away with the Bears' starting job. The team cut his main competition, Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills. </p><p>Ozzy Trapilo could be the team's long-term answer at the position. He's been practicing with the team in full for more than a week but was a healthy scratch on game day Monday. The team is being deliberate with how they bring Trapilo back from injury after he suffered a patellar tendon tear during the Bears' playoff win against the Packers in January.</p>

entries.title: Bears notes: Rookie Dillon Thieneman gets first interception
entries.summary: <p>Bears first-round rookie Dillon Thieneman’s first interception came off the hand of only the second-most improbable quarterback to play Monday night.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-inactives-vs-eagles-k-cairo-santos-cb-tyrique-stevenson-good-to-go" target="_blank" >Eagles</a> backup Andy Dalton tried to throw to receiver Dontayvion Wicks on third-and-goal from the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ 2 in the second quarter. The Bears safety stepped between Wicks, who was running along the back left of the south end zone, and the ball. Thieneman, 22, was 7 years old when Dalton began his NFL career in 2011.</p><p>Thieneman, who slid to the ground for a touchback, kept the ball for himself, carrying it to the Bears sideline while being mobbed by his teammates.</p><p>The red-headed veteran — and one-time Bear — was only in the game because starter Jalen Hurts was hit late by linebacker D’Marco Jackson as he ran out of bounds four plays earlier. The NFL’s concussion spotter ordered Hurts to be examined.</p><p>Hurts returned for the next drive after being cleared and marched the Eagles to a touchdown at the end of the first half, running a quarterback sneak up the middle as time expired.</p><h3>No Tyrique</h3><p>Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was declared healthy for the game — and then wasn’t in his usual spot. Stevenson, whom the team said hurt his hamstring last week, participated in only one full practice this week — on Friday. He didn’t carry an injury designation.</p><p>He was nonetheless replaced by rookie Malik Muhammad, who started at Stevenson’s outside cornerback spot. With Muhammad outside, the Bears played Cam Lewis in the slot.</p><h3>Hold it</h3><p>The NFL’s special teams coordinators held a meeting Friday to discuss a loophole in the league’s new kickoff rule exploited by both the Falcons and Eagles earlier this season. The NFL allows teams to use a 12<sup>th</sup> player on kickoffs — a holder who keeps the ball straight before the kicker can boot it.</p><p>The intent of the rule was for the kicking team to use a tee in such situations. The Eagles didn’t in Week 2, which Bears special teams coordinator Richard Hightower said violated “the intent of the rule." On Monday night, they used a tee.</p><h3>Notes</h3><p>• Running back D’Andre Swift, who spent a year with the Eagles before signing with the Bears, was the team’s extra captain.</p><p>• Rookie tight end Sam Roush cost the Bears field position when he touched a punt that cornerback Josh Blackwell stopped at the 2. Roush sprawled out on the ground with his foot on the goal line, prompting the touchback call.</p>

entries.title: 'There's nothing greater than joy' — West Ridge synagogue celebrates Jewish holiday Sukkot
entries.summary: <p>Lively Hebrew music pulsed through the streets of West Ridge Monday night, announcing the celebration of the Jewish holiday Sukkot.</p><p>“It's the holiday of unity and joy," said Rabbi Baruch Hertz of Congregation Bnei Ruven synagogue, which held the event. "This idea of dancing in the street, bringing the joy not only to synagogue, not only to your family but actually to the street to bring the community together."</p><p>During the event, about a block of Whipple Street near Devon Avenue, outside Bnei Ruven, was closed to traffic for the night as dancers took over the road. Men in Orthodox dress and beards joined hands and danced in a circle as a live band played and children joined in dancing or played nearby. </p><p>Sukkot — also spelled Sukkos in some Orthodox communities — began thousands of years ago as a celebration of the harvest. It lasts seven days, beginning five days after Yom Kippur, the Jewish holiday of atonement and forgiveness. Traditionally, Jewish families build a temporary hut as part of the Sukkot celebration, Hertz said.</p><p>"There's nothing greater than joy," Hertz said. "People dance together and many don't know each other but they come for one purpose of connecting and celebrating, that brings a strong message of light and goodness to the world."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-860000" name="image-860000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/81e27c9/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7a%2F94%2Fd994ad6e4a3cbf8928b9f196a2b8%2Fdancinginthestreets-260929-2.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/1acb3d1/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7a%2F94%2Fd994ad6e4a3cbf8928b9f196a2b8%2Fdancinginthestreets-260929-2.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/8b42dd8/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6048x3394+0+319/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F7a%2F94%2Fd994ad6e4a3cbf8928b9f196a2b8%2Fdancinginthestreets-260929-2.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Singer Uzi Bodner performs on stage during Congregation Bnei Ruven's 32nd annual "Dancing in the Streets" on Monday, Sept. 28, 2026. entries.title: Bears jump on Eagles early, lead 10-7 at halftime without starting QB Caleb Williams
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> started hot Monday against the Eagles and are holding their own without starting quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/11/as-engineer-and-artist-blend-styles-bears-ben-johnson-gets-goosebumps-about-future-with-caleb-williams" >Caleb Williams</a>. They’re up 10-7 at halftime thanks to a strong first half by third-stringer Case Keenum and two turnovers by Philadelphia.</p><p>Keenum has completed 15 of 21 passes for 149 yards and a touchdown for a 107.0 passer rating.</p><p>The Bears got the ball first and went 66 yards for a touchdown, ending with Keenum’s shovel pass to Luther Burden in the backfield for the score. From the Eagles’ 8-yard line, Keenum threw underhand to Burden at the 12, then he appeared to be stopped at the 4, but tight end Colston Loveland and left tackle Braxton Jones pushed him the rest of the way to the end zone.</p><p>They had another chance to score when defensive end Austin Booker forced a fumble and safety Xavier Woods recovered it at the Eagles’ 15 late in the first quarter, but the Bears couldn’t turn that into points. They got inside the 1-yard line on Keenum’s pass to Loveland, but ultimately Keenum threw incomplete on fourth-and-goal from the 3.</p><p>The Eagles wasted an opportunity at the Bears' 1-yard line in the second quarter when backup quarterback Andy Dalton replaced Jalen Hurts for a few plays and threw an interception in the end zone to Dillon Thieneman. Hurts was being evaluated for a concussion after a late hit by Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson.</p><p>They scored just before the half, though, on a last-second quarterback sneak by Hurts at the goal line.</p><p>The Eagles will receive the ball to begin the second half.</p><h3>Here are the Bears’ inactives for the game:</h3><p>QB Caleb Williams (hamstring)<br>OT Ozzy Trapilo<br>OL Jordan McFadden<br>DL Jamree Kromah<br>DL Jayden Loving</p>

entries.title: For second straight year, Cubs tab Matthew Boyd as Game 1 starter in wild-card playoff series vs. Padres
entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> started veteran left-hander <b>Matthew Boyd</b> in Game 1 of their National League wild-card series against the Padres last season, a postseason-opening victory at Wrigley Field.</p><p>They’ve decided to run it back.</p><p>Manager <b>Craig Counsell</b> on Monday announced Boyd as the Cubs’ starter for Game 1 of the best-of-three wild-card rematch against the Padres, which starts Tuesday night at Petco Park.</p><p>Though his season was affected by a pair of injuries, including knee surgery that kept him out for nearly two months, Boyd finished the regular season with a 3.91 ERA in 22 starts. That was highlighted by a dominant stretch upon his return from that long layoff, during which he posted a 1.93 ERA in his first seven starts back.</p><p>That was followed by a bumpier stretch, but he finished with a 3.28 ERA in his last six starts.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">San Diego. Drink it in. It always goes down smooth. Just like these couple two tree things about the Cubs the night before the playoffs start. <a href="https://x.com/suntimes_sports?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@suntimes_sports</a> <a href="https://x.com/Suntimes?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@Suntimes</a> <a href="https://t.co/2j45VXUP43">pic.twitter.com/2j45VXUP43</a></p>— Vinnie Duber (@VinnieDuber) <a href="https://x.com/VinnieDuber/status/2104753348423622985?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>‘‘Playoff starts are a challenge,’’ Counsell said. ‘‘Matthew’s experienced in that, had good experiences last year for us, and we look for him to do the same [Tuesday].’’</p><p>The Cubs figure to be happy if they get a similar start to the one Boyd made against the Padres last postseason, in which he allowed one run in 4⅓ innings.</p><p>But starting pitching isn’t something that looks the same in the playoffs, and Counsell again was repeating his ‘‘out-getters’’ mantra on the eve of Game 1.</p><p>‘‘We’ve just got to figure out how to get 27 outs,’’ Counsell said. ‘‘The order that happens? Starter, reliever, closer, setup man — those words don’t matter. We’re just trying to get 27 outs.’’</p><h3>Gausman, Imanaga will pitch</h3><p>While veteran right-hander <b>Kevin Gausman</b> wasn’t selected as the Cubs’ starter in Game 1, Counsell said he will pitch during the series.</p><p>Gausman, who was acquired at the trade deadline, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/27/cubs-kevin-gausman-shoulder-injury-game-1-starter-playoffs-wild-card-series-padres-alex-bregman-third-base-pete-crow-armstrong-games-played-start-times" target="_blank" >banged up his left shoulder</a> on a diving tag play last week.</p><p>The same goes for left-hander <b>Shota Imanaga</b>, who threw 12 pitches in one inning Sunday against the Red Sox.</p><p>Counsell didn’t commit to either pitcher starting, but he said they’ll get into games somehow.</p><p>Gausman made five starts and one relief appearance for the Blue Jays during their run to the World Series last fall and knows what’s required in the postseason.</p><p>‘‘Whatever you think is going to happen, you don’t know what’s going to happen,’’ he said Sunday. ‘‘You’ve got to be ready for everything.</p><p>‘‘Guys are going to be asked to do things they haven’t been asked to do all season. If you’re not ready for it, it can mess with you. But you’ve got to change your mindset to, ‘The most important game of the year is on Tuesday, and if it takes 10 guys to get through that game, that’s what it’s going to take.’</p><p>‘‘You’re just living and dying by every day.’’</p><h3>Bregman at third base?</h3><p>Third baseman <b>Alex Bregman</b> might be limited to designated-hitter duty in the wild-card series. He is still not far removed from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/23/cubs-alex-bregman-face-injury-return-matt-shaw-bunt-daniel-palencia-stats" target="_blank" >taking a foul ball to the face</a> and suffering multiple facial fractures.</p><p>After Bregman took ground balls during a workout Monday, Counsell said the Cubs still have a decision to make about whether they want to risk exposing Bregman to further danger by playing him in the field in Game 1.</p><p>‘‘I’ll be honest, I haven’t made a decision there yet,’’ Counsell said. ‘‘[Monday] was a much better day than how he looked [Sunday] in Tampa. So that’s a good sign.</p><p>‘‘He still has fractures in his face, and that’s what we have to weigh. That’s a decision that we’ve got make overnight.’’</p>

entries.title: Bears' Caleb Williams can control fate of his QB class — whenever he returns
entries.summary: <p>Quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/09/28/qb-jj-mccarthy-trade-vikings-giants" >J.J. McCarthy’s trade to the Giants</a> on Monday was at the same time inevitable and shocking.</p><p>It was clear the La Grange Park native was out of the Vikings’ plans when they decided to make Carson Wentz their second-string quarterback to begin the season — and their starter in Week 2 against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>.</p><p>Still, trading the former No. 10 overall pick after he made just 10 starts is a shocking admission of a pick gone wrong. A year and two weeks ago, McCarthy made his first NFL start after being sidelined a year with a knee injury. He rallied the Vikings to a win against the Bears at Soldier Field and was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week.</p><p>He’s still young. At 23, McCarthy is five months younger than Ole Miss’ Trinidad Chambliss, who is considered one of the top passing prospects in the college game. Who gives up on that? And who does it for a fifth-round pick, the NFL equivalent of pocket change?</p><p>Monday’s trade was the latest indignity for the 2024 first-round quarterback class, which can boast Caleb Williams’ Week 1 highlight reel, Falcons quarterback Michael Penix’s standout season debut Thursday — and little else.</p><p>Williams pulled his hamstring last week and didn’t play <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/monday-night-football-what-to-watch-for-in-bears-eagles-when-each-team-has-the-ball" target="_blank" >Monday night against the Eagles</a>. He wasn’t put on injured reserve before the game, though, which means the Bears expect him to return within the next three weeks. The Week 5 game in Green Bay seems more likely of a target than Sunday against the Jets.</p><p>Williams played the best game of his career in Week 1 and one of the worst in Week 2. He’s still in better position than most of his classmates.</p><p>There was a time when the class had the potential to be one of the greatest ever. That time? The end of the last regular season.<br>Maye, the third pick of the draft, finished as the MVP regular-season runner-up last year.</p><p>Since then, he’s committed 15 turnovers dating to the start of last season’s playoffs. He has one touchdown pass and six interceptions this season. In the Patriots’ loss to the Jaguars on Sunday, he fumbled the ball without being hit, saying the team’s center made the ball bloody — and slippery.</p><p>He has a 58.6 passer rating this season, 31<sup>st</sup> out of all qualifying quarterbacks in a sport with 32 teams.</p><p>"I can't get out of my own way, personally,” he told reporters Sunday.</p><p>The Commanders’ Jayden Daniels, the second pick of the draft, dislocated his left elbow in Week 2. It marked the second time in four weeks, dating to last year, he dislocated the same elbow. He’s played just nine games in the past two seasons — and finished four of them. The Commanders didn’t put him on IR, hoping that he can return soon. But how will the team protect his elbow?</p><p>Former No. 12 pick Bo Nix, who quarterbacked the Broncos to the AFC championship game last year — which he missed due to injury, paving the way for Maye to advance — has a passer rating of 80.3 this season, which ranks 27th. He’s thrown four touchdowns and three interceptions.</p><p>The Falcons had lost their first two games by a combined 38 points when Penix, their surprise No. 8 selection, returned to face the lost-in-the-woods Packers last week. He went 18-for-25 for 257 yards and a 101.4 passer rating, giving hope to the Falcons — and a grateful nation, which has to watch them in prime time for each of the next two weeks.</p><p>And then there’s McCarthy, whose career never launched despite having quarterback guru Kevin O’Connell as his head coach. His next opportunity will come with former Bears head coach Matt Nagy, the offensive coordinator for the Giants. When that happens is anybody’s guess. Giants head coach John Harbaugh — whose brother Jim coached McCarthy at Michigan — said that he’ll be the second- or third-stringer as he learns the team’s offense. Jameis Winston, who has a 55.6 passer rating, will “be the starter for as long as I can see into the future," Harbaugh said. That’s far from a glowing endorsement.</p><p>McCarthy didn’t demand a trade. Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley said the team decided trading him for best for the franchise.</p><p>"You have to recognize when a different situation or a new opportunity presents itself that it has the opportunity to present better outcomes," he said.</p><p>After not being spotted by reporters at any point during or after practice last week at Halas Hall, Williams spent Monday night in a matching navy hoodie, sweatpants and cap with the Bear face on the front.</p><p>Whenever he returns from injury, he’ll have the fate of the Bears riding on his right arm — and right hamstring.</p><p>He’ll have the reputation of his draft class riding on him, too.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/nfl/2026/09/28/qb-jj-mccarthy-trade-vikings-giants" >Vikings trade QB J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a 2027 fifth-round draft pick</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: After ending his slump, White Sox slugger Munetaka Murakami is ready for a 'big, long postseason run.'
entries.summary: <p>HOUSTON — The last time the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" >White Sox</a> were in Houston, things took a turn for the worse.</p><p>“Not sure we were quite clicking on all cylinders,” said manager Will Venable. “They just beat us because they're a good team, and they played better than us.”</p><p>The Sox dropped three of four to the Astros to not only start the month of September, but to open a skid of 12 losses in 17 games that cost them the American League Central Division. Looking back on it , Sox players vary between hopeful to adamant that those results said more about where they were as a team, than how they match up against a middling, but battled-tested Astros team.</p><p>“We were in kind of a tough spot,” said outfielder Tristan Peters. “We don't really think about that series. And it doesn't matter who the opponent is, we're going to play our best baseball this postseason.”</p><p>All-Star first baseman Munetaka Murakami doesn’t like to dwell too much on that series either, but his 1-for-14, eight-strikeout showing at Daikin Park earlier this month was an inflection point. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/03/white-sox-keeping-luis-castillo-in-rotation-and-munetaka-murakami-high-in-batting-order-amid-struggles-will-venable-astros-road-trip-zach-bove-al-central-division-playoffs" target="_blank" ><u>He spoke at the end of the series</u></a> and admitted the attack angle of his swing had grown into too extreme of an uppercut, leading to more whiffs and lazy fly outs.</p><p>Things got worse before they got better. Murakami followed up the Astros series with a 4-for-40, 24-strikeout stretch that ran through the end of the Sox losing two of three in Cleveland in September, but the work to recalibrate was already underway.</p><p>“We showed him some information from when he was at his best, kind of an objective feedback presentation, and he took well to it,” hitting coach Derek Shomon told the Sun-Times of his message to Murakami. “This is what it looked like in the setup through the initial move, through the forward move, through contact, and this is what's gotten you away from it. Now take it and run with it.”</p><p>Murakami alluded to a correlated enhancement of his pre-existing leg strengthening routine that had his leg base feeling more stable in the batter’s box. After he hit .263/.378/.684 with four homers in his last 10 regular season games, Shomon believes Murakami is pretty close to full power, which is essential for the White Sox.</p><p>Miguel Vargas has been the club’s best player all year long. Chase Meidroth, recently battling a sore hamstring, has been the second-most valuable if you believe in advanced metrics <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/22/chase-meidroth-brings-fire-to-surprising-white-sox-team-colson-montgomery-kyle-teel-randal-grichuk-chris-getz-mike-vasil-derek-shomon-ryan-fuller-justin-jirschele" target="_blank" ><u>and/or the power of sheer grit</u></a>. But in the playoffs where teams are even more aggressive about bullpen deployment to stamp out potential rallies, game-changing home run power is more valuable than ever. And Murakami in full working order has the sort of pop that makes gawkers out of his fellow Sox hitters with over 30 homers.</p><p>“I hit behind him,” said Vargas. “When you see that ball coming off the bat from behind the plate, it’s unbelievable.”</p><p>“A lot of guys, [their homers] have to be pull-side, up in the air,” said shortstop Colson Montgomery. “We’ve seen a couple of them this year where it’s down-and-away fastballs and he just flicks them out to left field.”</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/09/25/white-sox-shortstop-colson-montgomery-sets-new-mlb-single-season-record-for-strikeouts-chase-meidroth-huascar-brazoban-chris-getz-mark-reynolds" target="_blank" ><u>While Montgomery has sputtered down the stretch</u></a> and fallen down the batting order, and Vargas has become a steadying force that the coaching staff rarely worries about, Murakami is still a uniquely domineering presence in the White Sox lineup. And with a righty-heavy Astros pitching staff outside of All-Star closer Josh Hader, Murakami is the sort of fearsome matchup Houston has little answer for if he’s right.</p><p>The last week of the season would suggest he is nearing such territory, but the Sox first baseman argues he’s entering new territory altogether.</p><p>“They've been talking about that, but it's a new start,” Murakami said via interpreter of his recent work with Sox hitting coaches. “It's a start for a new beginning again. A big, long postseason run.”</p>

entries.title: These four things could make the difference in Cubs’ wild-card playoff series vs. Padres
entries.summary: <p>SAN DIEGO — The playoffs have arrived.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> have been building to this all season long, eyeing a run deep into October.</p><p>‘‘This group is ready,’’ catcher Carson Kelly said Sunday. ‘‘It’s been a long year. We’ve had our ups and downs. But what this group does really well is we come prepared every single day.’’</p><p>To get to where they want to go, the Cubs first need to get past the Padres, their opponent in a best-of-three wild-card series.</p><p>Here’s what could make the difference:</p><h3>Pete Crow-Armstrong</h3><p>Crow-Armstrong has been the best player in baseball this season and soon will have an MVP award on his mantel to show for it.</p><p>But the individual accolades have meant little to Crow-Armstrong, given that he’s focused on team goals. The chase for the biggest of those — a World Series title — starts now.</p><p>It’s a team sport, and everyone will have to do their job for the Cubs to win. But if you’re going to talk about the impact one player can make, Crow-Armstrong <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/21/cubs-nl-wild-card-standings-mlb-playoffs-seeding-padrres-phillies-pete-crow-armstrong-40-40" target="_blank" >can make more than</a> just about anyone else in the playoffs.</p><p>‘‘We’re fortunate we get to see it in person every single day,’’ Kelly said. ‘‘There are a lot of times where we’ll look at each other and say, ‘Oh, my gosh, did that really just happen?’</p><p>‘‘Sometimes he gets up there, and you’re like, ‘OK, Pete’s going to hit a homer.’ He hits it, and you’re like, ‘What?’ Or running a ball down in the gap. Stealing a base, stealing second and third. You’re like, ‘This guy, he does it all.’ ’’</p><h3>Alex Bregman</h3><p>A week ago, the Cubs didn’t know what Bregman would be able to give them, if anything, in the postseason after <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/23/cubs-alex-bregman-face-injury-return-matt-shaw-bunt-daniel-palencia-stats" target="_blank" >taking a foul ball off his face</a>.</p><p>But not only are they able to include Bregman in their playoff plans, they can count him as a<br>centerpiece.</p><p>A week removed from his freak injury, Bregman <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/27/cubs-alex-bregman-face-home-runs-red-sox-mlb-postseason-playoffs-series-padres-world-series" target="_blank" >homered twice</a> as part of a four-hit Sunday.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">San Diego. Drink it in. It always goes down smooth. Just like these couple two tree things about the Cubs the night before the playoffs start. <a href="https://x.com/suntimes_sports?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@suntimes_sports</a> <a href="https://x.com/Suntimes?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@Suntimes</a> <a href="https://t.co/2j45VXUP43">pic.twitter.com/2j45VXUP43</a></p>— Vinnie Duber (@VinnieDuber) <a href="https://x.com/VinnieDuber/status/2104753348423622985?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Bregman got back to being Bregman in a hurry, and that’s a big deal. The Cubs signed him to a five-year, $175 million free-agent deal in part to be a force in October, where he’s <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/14/cubs-alex-bregman-career-playoff-games-postseason-world-series-braves-nl-wild-card-standings-mlb-playoff-matchups-carson-kelly-sprint-speed" target="_blank" >one of the most accomplished postseason hitters of all time</a>.</p><p>And showing some Chicago toughness helps, too.</p><p>‘‘It fires you up,’’ Crow-Armstrong said Monday. ‘‘Knowing him and how wonderfully crazed he is about his work and how much he loves the game, it’s not really surprising. Not to put a damper on how cool it is, him coming back after eight facial fractures and whatnot, I’m just not that surprised. He lives for this kind of baseball.</p><p>‘‘Most important, I’m glad he’s healthy enough to do what he loves. But selfishly, I’m pumped that he’s going to be in our lineup for these important games. Simply put, Alex Bregman makes our lineup better, so it’s huge he’s getting himself game-ready.’’</p><h3>The bullpen</h3><p>It wasn’t long ago that the Cubs’ bullpen was in disarray.</p><p>But things have stabilized a bit, with manager Craig Counsell leaning on right-handers Ryan Zeferjahn (1.13 ERA in his last nine outings) and Daniel Palencia (eight scoreless appearances in a row) to great effect.</p><p>Palencia is looking more like the guy who dazzled last season, and Zeferjahn is looking more like the guy the Cubs thought they landed in a deadline deal.</p><p>‘‘He’s had some good outings lately,’’ Counsell said of Zeferjahn. ‘‘I feel great about him. He’s going to pitch. He’s going to be a major part of this at the end here.’’</p><p>The Cubs don’t necessarily have a designated closer, not that they see that as a problem, given Counsell’s ‘‘out-getters’’ mantra. But should any fans fret that is the team’s Achilles’ heel, maybe Zeferjahn can put their minds at ease.</p><p>‘‘There’s ups and downs, and I rode that ‘down’ for a little bit,’’ Zeferjahn said. ‘‘But I’ve been working my way back up. . . . Hopefully, I’m riding an all-time high here going into the playoffs.’’</p><h3><b>The conditions</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Cubs led baseball in runs scored this season, but <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/09/26/cubs-regular-season-finale-playoffs-mlb-postseason-nl-wild-card-standings-offense-lineup-pitching-rotation" >the bats didn’t look great</a> last week, averaging just two runs a game.</p><p>But heading to San Diego could have its advantages.</p><p>Kelly compared trying to hit at Wrigley Field and Fenway Park last week — they scored nine total runs in five games at the cold, windy venues — “like you’re hitting into a fan.”</p><p>The Cubs moved indoors Sunday and scored six runs. That’s only one game, hardly an indicator of what’s to come. But not dealing with poor hitting conditions is one way to allow a capable Cubs lineup to flex its muscles.</p><p>The catch? They might have to get real muscly, as the Padres — quite used to hitting in nice weather — have been on a roll, with only one team in baseball (the Brewers) scoring more runs in September.</p>

entries.title: Prosecutors: Suspect charged with shooting 1-year-old accidentally pulled trigger on gun
entries.summary: <p>The boyfriend of a 1-year-old baby’s mother meant to pull the trigger on a power drill when he accidentally fired a gun, striking the baby in the back of the head, prosecutors said Monday.</p><p>Davaris Washington, 38, appeared in court Monday on charges of reckless discharge of a firearm, unlawful use of a machine gun, reckless conduct causing great bodily harm and possession of a firearm by a repeat offender. The baby was in critical condition after the Saturday shooting, police said.</p><p>Washington was ordered detained by a Cook County judge.</p><p>Washington invited the baby’s mother over to his apartment late Friday, and she brought the 18-month-old baby to his Chicago Lawn home in her car seat. When she arrived at the apartment in the 6400 block of South Mozart Street, she placed the car seat between two couches in Washington’s living room, prosecutors said.</p><p>Washington picked up a gun with his left hand and a cordless drill with his right hand, then walked into the living room. He “attempted to rev the drill in order to determine if it was too loud for the sleeping baby,” according to prosecutors. But he pulled the trigger of the gun instead.</p><p>The firearm was equipped with a switch that allowed it to fire multiple rounds with one pull of the trigger. Washington allegedly fired three rounds, leaving bullet holes in parts of the couch and car seat, prosecutors said.</p><p>The baby was sleeping in her car seat when she was struck in the back of the head, prosecutors said. The baby’s mom picked her up and saw blood coming from the back of her head, initially thinking a gunshot was fired through the windows from outside.</p><p>Washington called 911 and asked the baby’s mother to hide the gun, but didn’t tell her what had happened, prosecutors said.</p><p>Police arrived at the scene and detained Washington. They recovered three shell casings, .45 caliber bullets and the gun, which was in Washington’s neighbor’s apartment, prosecutors said.</p>

entries.title: New crosswalk beacon, other signal upgrades intended to make Ridge Avenue intersection safer
entries.summary: <p>A dangerous Edgewater intersection may be made safer soon, as officials broke ground Monday on a new crosswalk beacon — the first of its kind being installed in the city. </p><p>Located where Ridge, Wayne and Hollywood avenues intersect in Edgewater, the signal is called a hybrid beacon; it acts as a traffic light but activates only when a pedestrian pushes the call button, according to the the Chicago Department of Transportation .</p><p>Officials attending the groundbreaking said they hope it will help residents safely cross the intersection, which currently has no traffic signals. The hybrid beacon should be ready by spring.</p><p>“We, in the city of Chicago, do not want to see another death to make our crosswalks safe,” said Ald. Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth (48th), who attended an afternoon groundbreaking ceremony at the site. </p><p>The $1.3 million project comes about five years after a pedestrian died in a 2021 crash at the intersection. The death of 63-year-old Sharon Lowrie sparked calls for traffic safety reforms from the community.</p><p></p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-df0000" name="image-df0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/26183b7/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/60e955a/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/fb30d51/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Ald. Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth (48th) attending a news conference before a ground-breaking ceremony for a traffic safety improvements project at Ridge, Wayne and Hollywood Avenues on Monday, Sept. 28, 2026." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/fb30d51/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/0a14c40/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/fb30d51/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4204x2359+0+222/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fa0%2Fba%2Fa0e7a1824ae181fd3b30eb1f0220%2Ftrafficsafetycdot-260929-07.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Ald. Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth (48th) attended Monday’s news conference and groundbreaking for a traffic safety improvements project on Ridge Avenue in Edgewater.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Ashlee Rezin/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The beacon will have two red lenses above a single yellow lens. The yellow lens doesn't light up until a pedestrian pushes the button, according to Manaa-Hoppenworth's website. The beacon directs motorists to slow down and then stop as it changes from yellow to red. Pedestrians can then cross, and after a flashing countdown, the signal turns off. </p><p>Such beacons, also known as high-intensity activated crosswalk beacons, already are in use in several other states, including Arizona, Texas, Michigan. State Sen. Mike Simmons, D-Chicago, who was also on hand Monday, said the technology can reduce pedestrian crashes by 55% and overall crashes by 29%.</p><p>“These are real effects that are going to improve safety for drivers and pedestrians all along Ridge,” Simmons said. </p><p>The project initially gained momentum through advocacy efforts by the community, especially the Edgewater Triangle Neighborhood Association and the BARGE Neighbors block club.</p><p>Anthony Pence, who leads the neighborhood association, said residents have long felt unsafe trying to cross Ridge at that intersection. The death of Lowrie, who lived in the area, made them realize they must advocate for change and hold elected officials accountable, Pence said.</p><p>“I think it’s going to be a change for some people … but I’m very excited,” Pence said. “I think it will certainly make streets safer around here.”</p><p>The overhaul will streamline the five-way intersection into a standard four-way design. In addition to the new beacon, there will be other improved crosswalks and signs, as well as accessible pedestrian signals, which provide audible and tactile cues.</p><p>During construction, northbound traffic will be reduced to a single lane; southbound traffic will still use two lanes. Additionally, the sidewalk on the west side of Ridge will be closed. </p><p>The majority of the project is expected to be completed this year , with resurfacing and landscaping expected to finish by spring .</p>

entries.title: Ben Johnson snaps back, mocks internet fascination with his QB history: 'That was apparently a big deal'
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson gives the impression that he’s locked in his office all day designing plays, but he’s got at least a little sense of what’s being talked about in the press and on social media.</p><p>He was aware, for example, that leading up to his team’s game against the Eagles on Monday there were graphics circulating that pointed out it would be the first time he called plays for a quarterback who wasn’t the No. 1 overall pick.</p><p>With Caleb Williams out, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-inactives-vs-eagles-k-cairo-santos-cb-tyrique-stevenson-good-to-go" >the Bears thumped the Eagles 27-7 with 38-year-old third-stringer Case Keenum playing lights out</a>, and Johnson took a victory lap on it afterward.</p><p>When asked about the challenge of switching his offense from Williams, who has elite mobility, to a classic pocket passer like Keenum, he brought it up unprompted.</p><p>“Well, I’ve got a little history of that, of calling plays for someone not so mobile,” he said with a smile, referring to his time with Lions quarterback Jared Goff. “Now, I don’t have a history with someone that’s not a No. 1 pick, though. That was apparently a big deal.”</p><p>Goff was the No. 1 overall pick in 2016, and Williams went first overall in 2024. Keenum was one of the most prolific quarterbacks in college football history, but went undrafted out of Houston in 2012.</p><p>When he stepped in for Williams on Monday, Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns for a 110.8 passer rating. He added a goal line touchdown on a sneak, too, that buried the Eagles with seven minutes left.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson leaves QB options open as he weighs starting Case Keenum or Tyson Bagent vs. Jets
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ third-string quarterback Case Keenum had a monster game in the 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday, but coach <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/11/as-engineer-and-artist-blend-styles-bears-ben-johnson-gets-goosebumps-about-future-with-caleb-williams" >Ben Johnson</a> left things up in the air as far as who will start Sunday against the Jets.</p><p>It remains highly unlikely that starter Caleb Williams will be back from his hamstring injury by then, leaving Johnson to decide between Keenum and No. 2 quarterback Tyson Bagent.</p><p>That was an easy call leading up to the Eagles game, Johnson said, because Keenum was convincing in practice and Bagent didn’t clear the NFL’s concussion protocol until Sunday. He hinted, however, that Bagent is very much in consideration against the Jets.</p><p>“We’ll have a discussion as a coaching staff and we’ll see where we need to go from here,” Johnson said. “There was a reason why Tyson ended training camp as our No. 2 quarterback.”</p><p>That could be merely a misdirection considering Johnson used a similar line Saturday even though he said later he was fairly set on starting Keenum by that point.</p><p>Neither Keenum nor Bagent had started since 2023, and at 38, Keenum’s main role on the Bears the last two seasons has been to mentor Williams and Bagent.</p><p>He was excellent, though, against the Eagles. Keenum completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns for a 110.8 passer rating, plus a touchdown on quarterback sneak at the goal line.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears' Case Keenum has to remain QB1 until Caleb Williams returns from injury
entries.summary: <p>They played football Monday at Soldier Field.</p><p>It was football, wasn’t it? Even if Caleb Williams — leader of men, star of stars, hope of a generation, spectator in a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> ball cap, hoodie and shades — wasn’t out there in the middle of it?</p><p>You’d better believe it was. It was good football. At times, it was great.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-inactives-vs-eagles-k-cairo-santos-cb-tyrique-stevenson-good-to-go" target="_blank" >A 27-7 win against the Eagles</a> will be remembered as the Case Keenum game, a 38-year-old has-been and never-was delivering on a prime-time stage like a man two-thirds his age and with triple the talent.</p><p>That might be a bit heavy on the hyperbole given how long a career Keenum has had and how respected he is, but it would be impossible to overstate the extent to which he exceeded expectations during three of the finest hours of his NFL experience.</p><p>“This is going to go down as one of the more special nights of my life,” Keenum said.</p><p>It isn’t wrong — at all — to surmise that Keenum lifted his team to a 2-1 record with more than just his throws that kept the ball moving down the field and the calm demeanor that was necessary in a test against a formidable opponent. He also pumped belief into an offense that needed it and attitude into a team that, coming off a 9-3 loss to the Vikings, needed it.</p><p>When Mad Hatter coach Ben Johnson went for it on fourth-and-goal from the 3 and the Bears missed, having shunned a chance at an easy field goal and a two-score lead in the early going, it came off as a brazen misjudgment. But Johnson had Keenum. Maybe the coach knew it wasn’t the risk it seemed with Williams out and No. 2 QB Tyson Bagent still not far enough removed from a concussion to start the game.</p><p>Williams remains out with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, but for how much longer? Another week or two or three? Until he comes back, just keep rolling with Keenum. Squeeze every drop he has left in his football body. Bagent’s time can wait, or continue to wait. Harsh, but the right way to go.</p><p>The sentiments in the previous paragraph come almost out of nowhere. Bagent is a good backup many teams would love to have. The Bears aren’t paying him $5 million a year because they don’t believe in him. Playing when Williams can’t literally is Bagent’s job.</p><p>But Keenum just turned things that upside-down.</p><p>Keenum doesn’t possess a howitzer of an arm, doesn’t sprint 20-plus mph to paydirt, hasn’t authored fourth-quarter comebacks galore. He isn’t Williams; isn’t close. He might not be Bagent. But he has earned the next start against the Jets, assuming Williams isn’t ready.</p><p>Ten years ago with the Rams, Keenum, a good soldier, kept the starting job warm for half a season until No. 1 overall draft pick Jared Goff was ready to take over. Now, still a good soldier, he can keep it warm for Williams for a bit.</p><p>“There’s so much emotion,” Keenum said. “Man, these guys that I’m with in this locker room, it’s incredible.”</p><p>Who knew he had it in him?</p><h3><b>MAKING THE GRADE</b></h3><p><b>QUARTERBACK — A</b></p><p>Case Keenum got the ball out fast, spread it around — eight different receivers caught passes in the first half alone — threw for two touchdowns, snuck in from the 1-yard line for another, injected his team with obvious confidence and, let’s face it, accomplished far more than any of us had reason to believe he would or could. Yes, the Eagles did him a solid by failing to deliver on possible chances for interceptions, but it was Keenum’s night. How ’bout that?</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">LUTHER BURDEN III TOUCHDOWN ON THE OPENING DRIVE!<a href="https://x.com/PHIvsCHI?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@PHIvsCHI</a> on ESPN<br>Stream on <a href="https://x.com/NFLPlus?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">@NFLPlus</a> <a href="https://t.co/nIcigJhv1e">pic.twitter.com/nIcigJhv1e</a></p>— NFL (@NFL) <a href="https://x.com/NFL/status/2104729493122498971?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 29, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p><b>RECEIVERS — B-PLUS</b></p><p>Rome Odunze’s end-zone drop was a bummer. Tight end Colston Loveland had a touchdown, then didn’t — stretch out those long arms at the goal line, dude! — but at least he finally reappeared with some catches. Kalif Raymond continues to make every play and might be the most underrated player on the team. Luther Burden was a big factor early and made the play of the game, taking a shovel pass in for a score from the 8, his legs churning inside a scrum of defenders while lineman Braxton Jones plowed the pile forward — it was glorious.</p><p><b>RUNNING GAME — C-PLUS</b></p><p>The Bears couldn’t prevent D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai from getting hit in the backfield until holes started to open up a bit — just a bit — in the second half. Still, grinding out the fourth-quarter clock with the ground game was a great way to end things and had to feel good. Sometimes you just have to keep at it. Swift ended with 84 hard-earned yards on the ground.</p><p><b>DEFENSE — A</b></p><p>On another night, the Eagles’ ability to run Saquon Barkley would’ve been a bigger problem. Not on this night. The Bears more than made up for any softness up front by getting pressure on QB Jalen Hurts — Montez Sweat and Dayo Odeyingbo got him for sacks — and, more important, by taking the ball away three times. Congrats on interception No. 1, rookie safety Dillon Thieneman, and in the end zone, no less. Linebacker Devin Bush wrapping up Tank Bigsby so Austin Booker could pile in and punch the ball out was picture-perfect.</p><p><b>COACHING — A-MINUS</b></p><p>What a bounce-back for Ben Johnson, who had a good-to-go offensive game plan dialed up after the debacle against Minnesota. Johnson believed in Keenum — believed the two of them could make it work together — and he was right. Just like that, Johnson looks like a guy with a heck of a gift again. Passing up a field goal in the first half wasn’t his finest hour — a 10-0 lead would’ve beaten the heck out of 7-0 at the time — but that’s just him. Even with his No. 3 QB in there, he’s never going to be afraid to go for it.</p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>Who starts at QB for the Bears? </b>Until we see Williams run out there again, this is story No. 1.</p><p><b>Flip that turnover switch: </b>The Bears can beat anybody when they win the turnover battle 3-0. They certainly can win the division again if they make a habit of it.</p><p><b>Thieneman has arrived: </b>Where does the first-round pick go from here? So far, it has been very promising.</p>

entries.title: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni: 'Remorse' for screaming at Bears LB D'Marco Jackson after late hit on Jalen Hurts
entries.summary: <p>A key sequence in the second quarter of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>' <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/09/28/bears-inactives-vs-eagles-k-cairo-santos-cb-tyrique-stevenson-good-to-go" >27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday</a> included Philadelphia coach Nick Sirianni screaming what appeared to be vulgar insults at Bears linebacker D'Marco Jackson.</p><p>Jackson was penalized for a late hit on Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts' scramble, and Hurts took such a hard shot on the play that he was required to come out of the game and be checked for a concussion. The Eagles sent in backup Andy Dalton, who ultimately threw an interception on third-and-goal at the Bears' 2-yard line.</p><p>After the play that forced Hurts out, ESPN's cameras showed Sirianni yelling at Jackson.</p><p>"You want to always fight for your players and protect your players, [but] I always come away, when I have a moment like that, with remorse," Sirianni said. "I shouldn’t let my emotions get the best of me. Those guys are out there trying to make a play. It was close on the sideline. It ended up being a penalty. You never want to see your quarterback get hit like that.</p><p>"But it's in the heat of the moment. Nobody's trying to hurt anybody out there. And I always have remorse when I act that way, but I always love fighting for our players. I love our guys. The emotion of the game probably got the better of me, and I have to learn from that particular moment. I have to be more steady in that situation... I didn't like how I handled that.”</p><p>Hurts returned on the next possession, but Dalton's interception (caught by rookie safety Dillon Thieneman) did significant damage by preventing the Eagles from tying the game. Instead, the Bears held the lead from the start and spent much of the second half up two scores.</p>
